Thorium breeder reactors (all nuclear power, really) blow solar power the fuck away.

They could be, but I really don't think it will happen.

Oil companies are still putting too much money into politics for that to happen, and the alternative technologies are still under-developed. Hydrogen fuel cells, in addition to still being relatively unstable, require special facilities to be built for refueling, and electric cars still rely on batteries, which are far more harmful in the long run to produce than simply burning fossil fuels.

Solar and wind are always proposed as the catch-all solution to these problems, but there are still concerns with solar/wind farms, both for nature and for people. Birds don't know the rate at which the blades of a windmill spin, and so attempt to fly through them, only to get hit by the next blade. Arrays of solar panels require us to use land that could instead be used for reforestation, farming, or numerous other uses. Solar power plants that reflect light to a central water tank can be improperly focused and temporarily blind helicopter and airplane pilots that fly too close to them. Even if not for these flaws, the weather is a fickle creature, and can have days with no wind, rendering wind farms useless, or days on end with thick cloud cover, rendering solar power useless. Both of these flaws require backup power systems that run on batteries or other means.

Germany actually tried to go full solar, and on cloudy days and at night when the solar panels were no longer generating power, the draw spikes on the European power grid were enormous - extra fossil fuel plants had to be built that could be turned on during certain times of day to accommodate the waves of houses suddenly drawing on the power grid that hadn't before then.

Nuclear power is really our best option for ditching fossil fuels, but governments and the people under them are too afraid of what might happen to a nuclear plant, despite the fact that the only nuclear disasters that have occurred at plants were design flaws that have either been fixed in the generations of nuclear power plants since those plants were first built, or in the case of Fukushima, a flaw that could not have been accounted for - a tsunami larger than any in recorded history actually reaching the plant, which was a good ways inland, and flooding the backup generators to keep the coolant running through the plant. The last nuclear accident before that was Chernobyl. Even then, had the Fukushima plant been a newer design (Generation 4 or Generation 5), the airflow around the cores would have been sufficient to keep them from melting down before they could get the backup generators online.

Conclusion: Even though in theory we could stop using fossil fuels, the only viable alternative is being held back for all the wrong reasons, and the other alternatives have nearly as many flaws as fossil fuels, if not more.

I started using oil cleansing about 4 months ago and I have the healthiest skin I've ever had so I am going to share what I do and a little about oil cleansing. Note: I am not a dermatologist and results may vary. I am just sharing info I have found on the web and what works for me :)

Theory:

  1. 'Like dissolves like' is a fundamental principal of chemistry and so you can use clean oil to 'dissolve' the dirty non-polar oils and sebum and make-up that builds up on your face.

  2. Oil cleansing replaces the natural oils that it removes so the face isn't stripped and dried out which can then cause overproduction of oil resulting in oily skin and acne.

  3. Specific oils can be utilized for their individual properties such as likeness to sebum, antibacterial properties, or skin soothing properties.

When done properly and consistently, the OCM can clear the skin from issues like oily skin, dry skin, sensitive skin, blackheads, whiteheads and other problems caused by mild to moderate acneâ€“while leaving your skin healthy, balanced and properly moisturized.

How to use OCM: I use this every evening or night. In the morning I only use a hot, wet washcloth to wipe my face.
1. Mix your oil. Don't mix a huge quantity as you may want to adjust as you find what works and what doesn't.
2. Rinse face with warm-hot water.
3. Use fingertips to massage oil into face. Use upwards circular motions, never pull skin down.
4. Thoroughly rinse/wipe off oil using a clean wash cloth and very warm water.
5. Use normal lotion or night cream or serum.

Mixing your oil: The trick with OCM is to figure out ones best oil mix which can take some trial and error and some education on the different properties of oil. However, the basic principle for mixing is to use a carrier, an astringent, and essential oils that have specific desired health properties.

The majority of the mix is the carrier oil. The secondary ingredient is the astringent. The essential oils should be no more than 3% of the mixture. Try adding 3-12 drops per oz, starting small and working your way up.

Carrier oils make up at least 70% to up to 97% of the mix. More than one can be used but don't get carried away. It's better to keep things simple with OCM. Here are some options:

-Sweet Almond or Apricot Oil: any skin type (apricot oil is one of my favorites) -Sunflower Oil or Argan Oil: regular skin.
-Avocado Oil: dry skin.
-Jojoba Oil: for all skin types (This is my favorite and what I use, it mimics sebum and so it regulates the bodies natural oil production. This is especially helpful for acne prone skin) -Hemp Seed Oil: for any skin types.

Astringent oils 30-20%: OR LESS for dry skin. For very dry skin, these can be left out or introduced in small, increasing quantities until an optimal level is reached.

-Castor Oil: all skin types, great for acne but the most drying so use in moderation, start low and build. If you use this and your skin seems dry, dial it down. Can be hard on sensitive skin.
-Grape Seed Oil: any skin type, oily skin.
-Hazelnut Oil:all skin types.

Essential oils 3%-ish or 3-15 drops per oz. These offer the most variety. There are hundreds of options with a wide variety of benefits varying from antibacterial properties to pleasant smell to wrinkle reduction, ect. Make sure you buy therapeutic grade oils that say they are ok to use on the skin. Read reviews, sometimes oils are fake or watered down. Here is a very small list of some and their supposed properties:

-Tea tree oil: anti-bacterial, regulates oil production (most commonly recommended for acne, I have seen ppl w/ cystic acne rave at the positive results) -Frankincense Essential Oil: anti-bacterial, anti-inflammatory benefits, natural toner (decreases pore size), cytophylactic (encourages cell renewal)
-Geranium Essential Oil: regulate oil production, anti-aging
-Lavender Essential Oil: beautiful, relaxing, and de-stressing smell
-Myrrh Essential Oil: anti-aging, soothes chapped, rashy, irritated skin
-Neroli Essential Oil: cytophylactic, easy on sensitive skin
-Patchouli Essential Oil: anti-aging, anti-bacterial and anti-fungal
-Rose Essential Oil: anti-microbial and anti-inflammatory compounds, reduces redness, improves tone and texture, smells great
-Ylang Ylang Essential Oil: anti-aging, wonderful smell

Here is a little chart of some of the more commonly recommended EOs for skin care.

Some notes:
-Anything new being introduced to the skin should be patch tested for 24hrs on the inside of the elbow (a sensitive area) to check for reactions.
-DO NOT use olive oil or coconut oil. Some blogs recommend these for the carrier oil but both cause breakouts!! Stay away.
-Redness, sensitivity, rashes and red, watery eyes are signs of allergy. Stop using the mix if these develop until the culprit can be identified.
-It may take 2-4 weeks to see results.
